title: Early Corticosteroids in Severe Influenza Pneumonia, a phase III randomized controlled trial
official: ECSIP : Early Corticosteroids in Severe Influenza Pneumonia, a phase III randomized controlled trial
summary: Main objective: To compare the efficacy of dexamethasone versus placebo in patients with severe influenza on a hierarchical composite endpoint of all-cause mortality, number of ventilator-free days and number of ICU-free days between day 0 and day 28.
conditions: patients with influenza-induced acute hypoxemic respiratory failure

interventions.name: DEXAMETHASONE VIATRIS 20 mg/5 ml, solution injectable en ampoule
CHLORURE DE SODIUM 0,9 % LAVOISIER, solution pour perfusion

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Age ≥ 18 years
2. Admission to ICU or intermediate care for less than 2 days
3. Admission to hospital for less than 5 days
4. Diagnosis of influenza pneumonia with •	PCR positive for Influenza dated less than 5 days •	AND focal shadowing/infiltrates on chest X-ray or CT-scan •	AND at least one of the following: cough, purulent sputum, chest pain or dyspnoea
5. Requirement of supplemental oxygen at a flow rate of at least 3 L/min OR non-invasive ventilation OR high flow oxygen therapy OR invasive mechanical ventilation.
6. Written informed or emergency consent
7. Ongoing medical insurance
Exclusion criteria:
1. Moribund state
2. Patient at risk of strongyloidiasis
3. Subject with shock on enrolment and on ongoing vasopressor therapy (≥ 0.25 microg/kg/min)
4. Indication for corticosteroid therapy in a dosage above 0.5 mg/kg/day prednisone-equivalent
5. Subject deprived of liberty or under a legal protective measure (example: patients under guardianship or curatorship)
6. Pregnant or breastfeeding woman
7. Lack of clinical equipoise by the attending physician and/or the presence of a substantial risk associated with the patients’ participation in the trial.
8. Bone marrow transplant or chemotherapy-induced neutropenia
9. Known allergy to dexamethasone or to one of its excipients
10. Uncontrolled psychotic states
11. Pheochromocytoma
12. Co-infection with COVID-19
13. Cardiogenic shock secondary to influenza myocarditis
14. Known active tuberculosis or fungal infection
15. Active viral hepatitis or active herpes virus infection
